trace.question: Name schools in Riverside which the average of average math score for SAT is grater than 400, what is the funding type of these schools?
trace.evidence: Average of average math = sum(average math scores) / count(schools).

attempts.sql:
SELECT s.School, s.FundingType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.County = 'Riverside'
  AND sat.AvgScrMath > 400

SELECT s.School, s.FundingType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.County = 'Riverside'
GROUP BY s.CDSCode, s.School, s.FundingType
HAVING AVG(sat.AvgScrMath) > 400

verdicts.text:
The query filters individual SAT rows instead of aggregating per school. The external knowledge defines the metric as an average of average math scores, so the query needs to group by school and filter on `AVG(AvgScrMath) > 400` in a HAVING clause.

```sql
SELECT s.School, s.FundingType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.County = 'Riverside'
GROUP BY s.CDSCode, s.School, s.FundingType
HAVING AVG(sat.AvgScrMath) > 400;
```

trace.final_sql:
SELECT s.School, s.FundingType
FROM schools AS s
JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.CDSCode
WHERE s.County = 'Riverside'
GROUP BY s.CDSCode, s.School, s.FundingType
HAVING AVG(sat.AvgScrMath) > 400
trace.answer: The results don't confirm which schools meet the SAT math criterion. Only River Springs Charter has a funding type listed (Directly funded). The other schools shown, such as La Sierra High and Banning High, have no funding type (NULL), and many rows are blank.
